To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two isomeric hydroxy(methoxycopper(I)) intermediates are produced in the reaction of CuO2 with CH4 in solid Ar and that the reaction mechanism is proposed to proceed via a series of elementary steps that include (i) O-O bond cleavage, C H bond activation by insertion of the oxygen atom into the CH bond, and H and CH3 transfer.

the CH3OH formation from CuO2 and CH4 is initiated by the O O bond cleaving to form the CH3OCO intermediate and then CH3OCuOH via C H bond insertion, and the CH3OCOH and CH3OCu-OH are isomeric and are not thermodynamicaly distinguishable.

two isomeric hydroxy(methoxycopper(I) intermediates were identified and characterized by matrix-isolation infrared spectroscopy and theoretical methods, and the mechanism of methane activation was proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanistic understanding of the direct methane activation to methanol, which has a great potential for the conversion of methane to methanol, a valuable feedstock for the chemical industry.
the mechanistic understanding of methane activation, which is an essential step for its conversion to methanol.
the mechanistic aspects of methane activation by CuO2 in solid Ar, which provides insight into the catalytic conversion of methane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the simultaneous formation of the cis and trans CH 3OCu(O H ) intermediates is a result of the competition between H and CH 3 transfer from the CH 3OC u O H to the CuO 2 species, which is the key to the formation of methanol in the Cu catalyzed conversion from methane to methanol.
the reaction mechanism is not only a thermodynamic one, but a dynamic one as well.
the CH3CuOH isomerization barrier is small enough to allow both isomers to form simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the formation and characterization of two hydroxy(methylcopper(I) intermediates, cis and trans CH 3OCu(O H), in the copper catalyzed methane to methanol transformation, and we have proposed the reaction mechanism for their formation.
the reaction of methane with copper cored oxidant is initiated by the insertion of the oxidant into one of the methane C H bonds.
the CuO2 species is the active oxidant for the direct conversion of methane to methanol and the hydroxy(methyloxy)copper(I) species is the active intermediate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CH3 group is not a spectator during the activation of methane by a copper cored oxidant.
the CH3OH formation pathway can be initiated by the CH3OCuc(OH) isomerization and that both isomers can be formed simultaneously.
the simultaneous formation of two isomers of CH3OCuOH can be explained by the presence of two transition states that lead to the same products.
